title: C26 Q8: CVD divergence as the CoinGlass CVD page draws it, with Malkan's 12-18 candle rule, on 1m/5m/15m/60m bars

what.name: CVD
what.value_plain: cumulative volume delta from Binance spot taker buy minus taker sell volume per 1m bar, summed to the bar size
what.label: OURS

what.name: Divergence
what.value_plain: price makes a higher high (lower low) while CVD makes a lower high (higher low): pivots +-3 bars, counted at the confirmation close, two legs 2-60 bars apart
what.label: OURS

what.name: Legs apart 12-18
what.value_plain: Malkan's rule for a valid divergence (QRIPTAL / Malkan extracts)
what.label: SOURCED

what.name: Hit
what.value_plain: the close 12 bars after confirmation moved the divergence's way; compared with the base rate of all 12-bar moves
what.label: OURS

what.name: Outcome read at the take-outs
what.value_plain: single short: first 15m close back under H1, stop H1 + 1.0 %, target L1, 24h, fee-net
what.label: OURS

what.name: Costs
what.value_plain: 0.10 % per round trip (Binance taker x2, backtest/fees.py); slippage and funding not modelled
what.label: SOURCED

verdict.label: Design look: on every bar size the hit rate sits at the 12-bar base rate; a 15m bear divergence stood within 4 bars of 2 of 30 take-outs

why: Hundreds of divergences fire per bar size and leg gap; their hit rate is the base rate of the market moving that way, so the signal alone carries no edge on this window.
At the C26 take-outs the divergence is rare (2 of 30), so it cannot be a Phase 3 filter; it stays a chart-reading aid.
Malkan's 12-18 bar rule is SOURCED; the pivot width, the +12-bar hit and the bar sizes are OURS.
